title: Modi Urges Global UPI Expansion as India Secures 'A' Sovereign Rating After 30 Years
excerpt: At Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai, the Prime Minister cited 7.8% GDP growth and UPI's 24 billion monthly transactions as proof that India's reform momentum is unstoppable.
body:
• PM Modi inaugurated the Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai, citing India's 7.8% GDP growth in the April-June quarter as evidence of economic resilience amid global uncertainty.
  • A Japanese credit rating agency upgraded India's sovereign rating to the A- category for the first time in three decades, which Modi called a validation of structural reforms.
  • UPI, which turned 10 on August 25, processed over 24 billion transactions in August alone and is now live in 11 countries, with Modi urging deeper integration with partner nations' payment systems.
  • Modi outlined a four-point roadmap for fintech — cybersecurity, ethical data protection, a regulatory innovation ecosystem, and a consumer protection index — and called on the sector to harness agentic AI, tokenization, and quantum computing.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday challenged India's fintech sector to push the Unified Payments Interface far beyond payments and into credit, insurance, and pensions, as he opened the Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai with a sweeping defence of the country's economic trajectory.

In his third consecutive keynote at the four-day conference — organized by the Payments Council of India, the National Payments Corporation of India, and the Fintech Convergence Council at Jio World Centre — Modi contrasted what he called a "phase of conflicts and uncertainties" worldwide with India's 7.8 percent GDP expansion in the April-June quarter.

"The world is going through a phase of conflicts and uncertainties. Even within this, the quarter from April to June has been the most challenging. And within that, when India grows at 7.8%, the world gains a new confidence."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India

Sovereign Rating Milestone

Modi highlighted a recent upgrade by a Japanese credit rating agency that moved India's sovereign rating to the A- category — the first time the country has achieved an A-level rating in three decades. He attributed the milestone to sustained structural reforms and macroeconomic stability.

"Only a few people know that this fortunate time has come after three long decades," Modi said, adding that the "reform express" would accelerate further. The upgrade bolsters India's case for cheaper international borrowing and greater foreign institutional confidence at a time when global capital flows remain skittish.

UPI at 10: From Scepticism to 24 Billion Transactions

Marking UPI's tenth anniversary — celebrated on August 25 — Modi traced the platform's arc from early scepticism among banking elites to its current status as the backbone of India's digital economy. The system processed over 24 billion transactions in August alone, with roughly 50,000 transactions executed in the first ten minutes of the event, according to the Prime Minister.

UPI is now live in 11 countries and has drawn praise from world leaders, including French President Emmanuel Macron, who called it "not just a tech story" but "a civilizational story," Modi noted.

The Prime Minister directed the industry to move aggressively on cross-border integration, replicating the model already in place with Singapore. "Wherever Indians live in large numbers, wherever India trades on a large scale, whichever country in the world is ready to walk with us, we have to work to connect them all," he said.

Beyond Payments: Credit, Insurance, and Pensions

Modi argued that fintech's next frontier lies not in payments but in delivering credit, savings, insurance, and pension products to the millions of small businesses and gig workers who remain outside formal financial services. He cited the PM SVANidhi scheme, which brought millions of street vendors into the formal credit system and boosted their average annual income by over 20 percent.

Using the example of a small shop owner whose digital transaction history proves her business viability but who remains too small for a traditional bank loan, Modi urged the sector to design curated financial models for micro-enterprises. "I believe the next chapter of fintech will be written right here," he said.

AI, Quantum, and a Four-Point Roadmap

Looking ahead, Modi identified agentic AI, tokenization, and quantum computing as transformative forces for the financial sector. He laid out a four-point strategic roadmap: top-notch cybersecurity, ethical data protection standards, a robust regulatory innovation ecosystem, and a transparent fintech consumer protection index.

"If we test ourselves on these criteria, India's fintech sector can become a gateway of countless possibilities," he said.

What's Next

The Global Fintech Fest runs through September 11 and is expected to feature regulatory dialogues, startup showcases, and policy roundtables with participants from the Reserve Bank of India, SEBI, IFSCA, and NITI Aayog. The conference theme — "Potential to Impact: Agentic AI | Tokenisation | Quantum" — signals that emerging technologies will dominate the agenda as India seeks to extend UPI's success into new financial verticals and global markets.
nri_angle: Modi directed the fintech sector to integrate UPI with payment systems in countries where Indians live in large numbers, aiming to cut remittance costs for the world's largest diaspora.
